opening.text: Captain here. Two workstation reports and unexpected outbound traffic. Services are still running. We need to establish what connects those signals.

opening1.text: Captain here. The night shift has reported a sluggish workstation and unfamiliar remote sessions. Patient services are still available. Establish what happened, and keep the clinical teams informed before you disrupt their systems.

opening2.text: Captain here. An unusual supplier session and unfamiliar support-server connections need investigating. Generation is stable. Keep the maintenance environment separate from the operating plant, and confirm the route before widening containment.

opening3.text: Captain here. The booking portal is receiving unusual requests, and support staff have spotted unexplained server activity. Vessel operations continue. Build the timeline while the terminal still has room to work.

opening4.text: Captain here. We have unusual control-plane activity and an egress-cost spike, with no scheduled deployment to explain them. Follow the identity and its permissions. We need evidence of how access is being maintained.

opening5.text: Captain here. An unfamiliar session is using a trusted support identity, and a dependent application has reported unexpected access. Service remains available. Establish the scope before you disturb the connections other teams rely on.

opening6.text: Captain here. Anomalous privileged access has appeared before a busy public transaction window. Services are still available, but the trust boundary is uncertain. Verify the authority behind those actions and protect the public service.

opening7.text: Captain here. Unusual management access and intermittent service degradation have been reported. We do not yet know whether they belong to the same incident. Compare the timings before you join the signals into a single explanation.

opening8.text: Captain here. An unapproved remote session and configuration access have appeared in engineering support. Treatment remains within safe limits. Work with the operators, preserve the evidence, and keep every intervention inside the safety boundary.

opening9.text: Captain here. Unusual privileged activity and an unexpected export pattern have appeared before settlement. Establish the route, preserve the transaction record, and keep trusted processing available while you investigate.

firstFinding.text: That gives us our first confirmed finding. Keep the evidence and the assumptions separate.

connectedFindings.text: Two stages are confirmed. The incident is taking shape, but the remaining activity is still unconfirmed.

thirdFinding.text: Three stages are confirmed. Close the last gap before you call this complete. Keep the timeline consistent with the evidence.

unexpectedFinding.text: That is a confirmed finding, but not the prediction we set out to test. Update the timeline before changing the working reading.

pressure.text: Operational pressure is rising. Keep the service consequences in view as you make the next call.

serviceStabilising.text: Service continuity has regained some margin. Use that room to investigate carefully. An improving service picture does not establish that the activity has stopped.

failedCheck.text: The check did not complete successfully. That leaves a gap in the evidence, not proof that nothing happened. Review the conditions before you spend another turn on the same approach.

weakSignal.text: We have a low-confidence signal. Keep it as a lead, and look for a second source before treating it as a confirmed part of the incident.

newDevelopment.text: A new report has entered the picture. Check what it actually changes: the evidence, the pressure on services, or the time available for the next decision.

noFinding.text: The check completed without confirming another stage. Keep the scope of that result clear. It tells us what this check found, not that the whole environment is clear.

noFindingAgain.text: Another check has left the next stage unconfirmed. Revisit the working reading and the source you are using. We need a check that can distinguish between the remaining explanations.

response.text: The four-stage chain is confirmed. We can now move through containment, assurance, and recovery.

assurance.text: The containment decision is recorded. Now test the boundary. We need evidence that the chosen response holds, and a clear account of the uncertainty that remains.

recovery.text: The assurance decision is recorded. Recovery is the next call. Restore service at a pace you can verify, and be explicit about any risk you are carrying forward.

won.text: Response complete. The incident is resolved. Review the record while the decisions are still fresh.

lost.text: The operation has ended with activity unresolved. Review what was confirmed and where the response lost its margin.

exercise.text: The controller has confirmed authorised exercise activity. Stand down and review what the investigation established.
